newsitem.title: UK: World LPG pauses for breath as U.S. prices slip.
newsitem.headline: World LPG pauses for breath as U.S. prices slip.

text.p: Worldwide Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) markets paused for breath this week after a period in which prices have risen relentlessly.
The decisive factor driving Europe recently has been the low level of U.S. propane stocks, traders said. But this week saw a dip in U.S. prices and European levels softened as a result.

"There's not much offtake in Europe at terminals as Europe has been stocking up and there's a lot in storage. And the U.S. market has tumbled a little this week, and mild weather has left buyers relaxed. The downside may be limited, but there's no upside in the short term,' said a Scandinavian trader.

The weaker tone was shown by deals during the week. A 10,000 tonne cargo was reported traded at $275 CIF French Atlantic coast, but the port was described as "difficult" and was said to equate to a level of $270 CIF ARA.
There were also two pieces of around 3,000 tonnes each reported done at $270 CIF Flushing. This compares with a price of around $278 a tonne CIF for large propane cargoes a week ago.

High European stocks are seen as limiting the speed with which prices are likely to move. "Even with cold weather it would take a little time for prices to change now, because inventories are so high" said a dealer.
